comments.body: I'd like to talk about eip 2926

i'd like to check in with everyone about this Fusaka timeline:

29 Aug: working fusaka trunk branches
3 Sep: fusaka-devnet-5 launch
10 Sep: fusaka-devnet-5 done -> use analysis to confirm [(target, max) values here](https://notes.ethereum.org/@jtraglia/fusaka_scheduling)
15 Sep: Holesky/Sepolia releases; bug bounty begins
22 Sep: Holesky forks
29 Sep: Sepolia forks
1-3 Oct: Hoodi and mainnet releases
8 Oct: Hoodi fork
5 Nov: mainnet

We currently have 18 PFI'd EIPs for Glamsterdam, with at least another month for people to make proposals. At 5-10 minutes per EIP on the call, if we get another 10ish, we're looking at 2-4 full ACDEs of PFI presentations. 

Teams are now sprinting towards Fusaka releases and (on the EL side) gas limit optimizations. I'm not sure this is the best time to shift our focus towards analyzing Glamsterdam proposals, but would want client teams to validate this. 

When/how is the best way to review all the PFI'd EIPs? Do we want to allocate time on the call to anyone who posts on the agenda, have client teams highlight the EIPs they'd most like to discuss, require EIP champions to provide async context ahead of the call, a combination? 

Would love to get teams' perspectives on this thread before Thursday's call. If time permits, and teams think it's a good use of time, then I'm happy to cover EIP-2926 (and potentially others!) @gballet 😄
Hey @timbeiko I'd like to speak a bit about EIP 7793 and 7843
If there's time I'd like to mention [EIP-8012](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/10218) and [EIP-8014](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/10220), should not take more than a couple of minutes.

> When/how is the best way to review all the PFI'd EIPs?

@timbeiko we should wait until the PFI deadline before reviewing, to avoid setting EIPs to Candidate for Inclusion without the context of all the PFId EIPs. 

The best way (IMHO) would be **async review and short listing by client teams and the community**, before short listed EIP champions can pitch at ACD.  

EIP authors/champions should ideally add a 5 minute presentation (video & slides) on how their EIP **significantly moves the roadmap forward** to their EIP discussions topic in Eth Magicians.
This could also ideally be surfaced on forkcast: https://forkcast.org/upgrade/glamsterdam#proposed-for-inclusion (@wolovim)
This would allow client teams & the community to review async. (without having to discuss on ACD).  [Ideas based on [my input to Pectra restrospective](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/pectra-retrospective/22637/2)]

An EIP would either need one or more client teams (ideally two) to nominate to short list and/or strong community signaling via forkcast (@wolovim time to bring back ranking)

Short listed EIP champions could then take 5-10 minutes of questions at ACD on how their EIP significantly moves the roadmap forward and have implementations & tests.

Client teams & the community could then writeup their preferences for CFI, summarized by the Protocol Support team (@nixorokish).  Then ACD can decide using this input.

re: glamsterdam non-headliners, ready to aid and further experiment with forkcast to support async education and signal gathering, but within ACD calls, perhaps scale it down to a 2-3 min "elevator pitch" with optional template questions. 5-10 minutes each is a lot, particularly if left unstructured.

> but within ACD calls, perhaps scale it down to a 2-3 min "elevator pitch" with optional template questions. 5-10 minutes each is a lot, particularly if left unstructured.

ACD time is too valuable for all the PFId EIPs to pitch, this needs to be an async review.
Only short listed EIPs should pitch at ACD, but agree, structure is important, and the shorter the better.
We probably want a couple of weeks of running post the holesky upgrade...

https://github.com/eth-clients/holesky/pull/129
https://github.com/eth-clients/sepolia/pull/110
https://github.com/eth-clients/hoodi/pull/19
https://github.com/eth-clients/mainnet/pull/10

Got some open PRs that we need to merge. These are needed in order for us to be able to do shadowforks. Please review them, deadline tomorrow.

The following are NOT Besu team preference, but instead EIPs that we would like to hear more about:

[EIP-5920](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-5920): PAY opcode: community feedback should be collected to make sure SC devs really want that

[EIP-7667](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7667): Raise gas costs of hash functions: community feedback required, because gas increases for existing contracts could break them, should be beneficial for Linea and other zk rolllups

[EIP-7791](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7791): GAS2ETH : Needs discussion and presentation, unclear when and how this would be used exactly

[EIP-7923](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7923): Linear, Page-Based Memory Costing: community feedback required, especially from compiler devs who are the ones who will most probably use it

If there is time, I would like to discuss the Glamsterdam Repricings Meta EIP. Specifically, I would like to understand if a Meta EIP is the desired format for organising the repricing work or not.
